The bakery had closed early, but the smell of orange peel still hung above the cooling racks. Beatrice stood beneath the stained ceiling with a roasting tin pressed against her chest. Each drop struck the metal loudly enough to make her blink. The ladder Ada had promised to return was still missing.

“If this gets into the flour, we close tomorrow too,” she said.

Leon pushed an empty rack beneath the stain. He had already taken off his good coat; it lay carefully folded on the clean end of the counter. “Put the tin here, Bea. Your arms are shaking.” He held the rack steady while Beatrice lowered her burden onto its top shelf.

At the back door, Priya shook rain from their sleeves. They set a canvas tool bag beside the oven and listened until another drop landed. The sound came a little later than the movement of the dark patch overhead.

“There's a space above that panel,” Priya said. “The water could be coming from the other end of the building.”

Beatrice looked toward the stairs. The upstairs tenant had complained about a loose window, but the room directly above them held only boxes. “I checked the window before I came down. The floor was dry.”

A key scraped in the front lock. Tomas entered sideways with a sheet of plywood, catching his heel on the mat. Leon reached for the nearer edge before it struck the display case.

“Don't put that under the leak,” Tomas said. He tilted the board toward the empty doorway. “It's for the window on the stairs. The glass is out.”

Beatrice put a hand on the counter. She had checked the wrong window.

“I thought you meant the one in the storeroom.”

Tomas rested the plywood against the wall. “I left a note on your bicycle.”

“My bicycle is at the repair shop,” she said. Her voice had gone quiet enough that Leon stopped brushing rain from the board.

Priya took a torch from the bag and aimed it at the ceiling, keeping the beam away from everyone's eyes. They waited for the others to look up.

“We can argue about bicycles when the water stops. Leon, can you hold the light?”

He took the torch, and Priya climbed onto the bottom step of the kitchen stool. Beatrice moved the flour sacks toward the oven. When the first sack proved too heavy, Tomas caught the other end without waiting to be asked. Above them, the patch spread past the edge of the panel.
